healthcareSystem: State-funded system undergoing reform. Tourists pay out-of-pocket. Private clinics in Kyiv and Lviv offer good quality care.
qualityNotes: Private clinics in Kyiv and Lviv provide good care with some English-speaking staff. Public hospitals have limited resources. Ongoing conflict affects healthcare access in eastern and southern regions.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-9pm; 24/7 pharmacies available in major cities
pharmacyTips: Look for 'Аптека' (Apteka) signs. Pharmacies are abundant in cities. Many medications available OTC that require prescriptions elsewhere. Pharmacists may speak basic English in Kyiv; less likely in smaller cities.
prescriptionRules: Many medications available OTC with relaxed enforcement. Antibiotics and some stronger medications technically require a prescription. Foreign prescriptions are generally not accepted. Visit a local clinic for a Ukrainian prescription if needed.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics (opioids, tramadol)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (benzodiazepines, stimulants)
restrictedMeds.note: Some ADHD medications and benzodiazepines are controlled. Bring documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis-based products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Ukraine in all forms, including medical marijuana and CBD products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, bring the original prescription. Having a Ukrainian translation is helpful but not required.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation is strongly recommended, especially given the ongoing conflict. Some insurers exclude Ukraine or specific regions. Verify your policy covers the areas you plan to visit. Medical evacuation to Poland or Germany may be necessary.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, Tdap — Ukraine has had measles outbreaks)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry. Ukraine has experienced measles outbreaks — ensure MMR vaccination is current.

waterNotes: Tap water in major cities is treated but often not recommended for drinking due to aging infrastructure. Use bottled or filtered water. Tap water is generally safe for bathing and brushing teeth in cities.
foodSafetyTips: Food in established restaurants is generally safe. Be cautious with street food and dairy products. Ukrainian cuisine is hearty and well-cooked. Wash fruits and vegetables before eating.
medicalTourismNote: Ukraine has been a destination for affordable dental care, fertility treatments, and cosmetic surgery. The ongoing conflict has significantly disrupted medical tourism.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Ukraine. Emergency 112, pharmacy tips, hospital info, vaccination advice, and travel insurance guidance.

hospitals.name: American Medical Center Kyiv
hospitals.notes: International clinic with English-speaking staff. General practice, emergency care, and specialist consultations.

hospitals.name: Boris Clinic
hospitals.notes: Modern private clinic network with multiple Kyiv locations. Some English-speaking doctors.

hospitals.name: Medicover Clinic
hospitals.notes: International clinic chain with English-speaking staff. Direct insurance billing available.

hospitals.name: Lviv Emergency Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main emergency hospital in Lviv. Limited English — bring a translation app.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available in Kyiv and Lviv at private clinics. Very affordable by Western standards.
dentalCare.costRange: $15-40 for a consultation; $25-80 for fillings; $20-60 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Ukrainian dental clinics, especially in Kyiv, offer quality care at a fraction of Western prices. Many dentists have trained in Europe.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, visit a private dental clinic (стоматологія). Most major cities have walk-in dental services.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: No dedicated English-language crisis line — contact your embassy
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Kyiv through international clinics and private practice. Sessions typically $30-60.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health awareness has increased significantly since 2022. English-speaking therapists are available in Kyiv but rare elsewhere.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is improving but remains limited. Kyiv has made progress with metro accessibility and public buildings.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private clinics are generally wheelchair accessible. Older public hospitals may lack elevators and ramps.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Kyiv Metro has limited accessibility (some stations have elevators). Newer buses are wheelchair-friendly. Taxis are the most reliable accessible option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Lviv's cobblestone streets and historic buildings present challenges for wheelchair users. Kyiv is more accessible. Plan routes carefully.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Masks are uncommon in public.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at private labs and clinics. Rapid tests: 200-400 UAH ($5-10); PCR: 800-1,500 UAH ($20-40).
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics may accept direct billing from major international insurers. Otherwise, pay upfront (cash, card, or USD accepted at some clinics) and keep all receipts and medical documents. Request English-language documentation. File claims with your insurer upon return.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Healthcare in Ukraine is very affordable by Western standards. Public emergency care is free but quality varies.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation to Poland is the most common route. Due to the ongoing conflict, evacuation plans should be arranged before travel. Some areas may be inaccessible for air evacuation.
